title: Ambient fibre stalk at the generic point of a coordinate subspace
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U an affine open of S, R=Γ(S,U), and s a prime of R. Let z be a point of A^a_S [def-sbc-affine-space] over the image of s, whose image in its scheme-theoretic fibre is generic. Write j:A^a_S→A^{a+b}_S for the coordinate inclusion retaining the first a coordinates and setting the last b to zero. Set k=s.ResidueField. There is a prime q of Frac(k[u_1,...,u_a])[v_1,...,v_b] [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], equal to the ideal generated by all v_i, and a ring equivalence from the stalk of the fibre of A^{a+b}_S at j(z) to the localization at q. No minimality hypothesis on s is needed; a=0 and b=0 are allowed.

proof.text: Identify the base residue field at the image of s with s.ResidueField using the affine-open residue-field isomorphism. The cartesian affine-space base-change square identifies each fibre with affine space over that field. The coordinate inclusion commutes with these identifications, by equality on its coordinate functions. Transport the tangential generic point and ambient stalk along these isomorphisms.

source.place: Scheme-theoretic fibres as residue-field base changes; affine-space base-change calculation from coordinate-chart witness Steps 3--4.

proof.text: Over the field k, the affine-space spectrum isomorphisms carry the generic tangential point to the zero prime. The coordinate inclusion induces evaluation of the last b variables at zero. Hence the ambient point is the kernel of this evaluation. Affine stalk localization identifies its stalk with localization at this prime. Relabel ULift coordinates by Fin.

source.place: Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves, part (6); coordinate-chart witness Steps 3--4.

proof.text: The sum-of-variable-types polynomial equivalence identifies k[u,v] with k[u][v], carrying this prime to the kernel of evaluation at v=0. Let R=k[u] and K=Frac(R). Polynomial localization shows K[v] is the localization of R[v] at the nonzero constant polynomials from R. The contraction of the origin prime in K[v] is the origin prime in R[v], by injectivity of R→K. Transitivity of localization therefore identifies their localizations. Polynomial induction proves that the evaluation kernel is the variable ideal. These constructions also apply to either empty variable type.

lean.statement:
theorem coordinate_subspace_generic_fiber_stalk
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (a b : ℕ) (U : S.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    (s : PrimeSpectrum Γ(S, U)) (z : AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin a)) S)
    (hz : (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin a)) S ↘ S) z = hU.fromSpec s)
    (hgen : IsGenericPoint
      ((AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin a)) S ↘ S).asFiber z) Set.univ) :
    let j := AffineSpace.homOfVector (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin a)) S ↘ S)
      (fun l : ULift.{u} (Fin (a + b)) ↦
        Fin.addCases (fun k ↦ AffineSpace.coord S (ULift.up k)) (fun _ ↦ 0) l.down)
    ∃ q : PrimeSpectrum
        (MvPolynomial (Fin b) (FractionRing (MvPolynomial (Fin a) s.asIdeal.ResidueField))),
      q.asIdeal = Ideal.span (Set.range (MvPolynomial.X : Fin b →
        MvPolynomial (Fin b) (FractionRing (MvPolynomial (Fin a) s.asIdeal.ResidueField)))) ∧
      Nonempty
        ((((AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin (a + b))) S ↘ S).fiber
            ((AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin (a + b))) S ↘ S) (j z))).presheaf.stalk
          ((AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin (a + b))) S ↘ S).asFiber (j z))) ≃+*
            Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
